notes: No official per-prefecture Korean visit-rate table (JTA 인바운드 소비동향조사 Table 6-1) could be opened; the PDF/Excel was not readable via fetch. The closest institutional signal is the 2025 JTA accommodation-night breakdown for Korean guests, which I only saw second-hand in Herald Economy (2026-09-23): Tokyo about 3.68M, Fukuoka about 2.88M, Osaka about 2.84M, Hokkaido about 2.38M, Okinawa about 1.15M nights (top 5 over 70% of Korean nights); Kyushu Korean share 35.8% (Oita 38.9, Fukuoka 36.8, Kagoshima 34.3, Saga 34.2); Ehime 42.4% highest in Japan. Arrival-by-airport figures (Osaka 2.49M, Tokyo 2.16M, Fukuoka 2.07M, Sapporo 0.82M, Naha 0.50M, Nagoya 0.35M, Tsushima 0.27M, Kumamoto 0.14M, Matsuyama 0.13M) come from a Daum/Nate blog compiling e-Stat, so treat as secondary; port/airport counts understate Fukuoka (Kitakyushu, Saga, Shimonoseki entries) and rank Osaka above Tokyo, whereas nights rank Tokyo first and Fukuoka above Osaka. Platform signals: MyRealTrip 2025 (Fukuoka top Japan city in flights, Osaka top in tours/tickets and accommodation); Agoda search 2025 (Tokyo, Fukuoka, Osaka top 3, Sapporo 8th); Skyscanner H1 flight searches (Fukuoka 2nd) were seen only in a search summary. National totals: 2025 Korean arrivals 9,459,6xx (+7.3%; one search snippet said +8.3%, treat 7.3% as correct per several outlets); 2026 Jan-Aug 7.42M (+21.2%). Attraction-level evidence is weak overall: there is no Korean-specific visitor-count table per attraction; the best items are Trip.com Korean-rating top 5 (Disneyland, DisneySea, USJ, Warner Bros Studio Tour Tokyo, Skytree) as relayed by a recruiting-site article of uncertain method, MyRealTrip homepage product order (single snapshot), and editorial lists (Travie, Trip.com blog, Tripstore) with no stated methodology. Many entries are qualitative blog/editorial mentions or all-nationality lists (giken.co.jp, Tripadvisor); I marked them weak or medium accordingly. Several fetches were paywalled or blocked (Nikkei details, honichi member sections, Tripadvisor 403, KKday 403, sikdorakuniv 403), so Klook/KKday/Triple full rankings, Kyoto and Hiroshima Korean-specific counts, and Nagasaki/Kagoshima/Hakodate numbers are missing. Klook survey (Korea Gen Z likes Fujinomiya and Niseko) is a stated-preference survey, not bookings. A Kumanichi headline mentions a July 2026 Kumamoto earthquake that sharply cut inbound visits to Kumamoto city; I did not verify details, so check before prioritizing Kumamoto. Kyoto is imposing tourist surcharges (lodging tax up to 10,000 yen, higher bus fares for non-residents) per Herald Economy 2026-02, which may affect trip patterns. Korean small-city interest (Matsuyama, Kumamoto, Shizuoka, Takamatsu, Hiroshima, Saga) is growing quickly but from a small base compared with Tokyo/Osaka/Fukuoka. Suggested Tier A candidates: Tokyo, Osaka, Fukuoka, Hokkaido (Sapporo/Otaru), Okinawa, Kyoto, Nagoya, Yufuin/Beppu, plus Matsuyama/Kumamoto as emerging.
